misconceptions.believed: That the way to keep abilities from dissolving the boss engine was to make them cost hit points -- the boss heals, so abilities are self-limiting.
misconceptions.revealed_by: Writing down how a fight is actually lost before writing the abilities, which the previous handoff told me to do first.
misconceptions.corrected_to: Hit points cannot end a fight. cmd_boss returns 1 when a step fails and can_repair is false; the boss's health is never consulted, and a boss at full health is a poor win rather than a loss. An ability priced purely in HP is priced in a currency the player can spend without limit -- healing a boss that is already full costs nothing, because Fight.remaining clamps at hp. So 'the boss heals 8' would have been free after the boss returned to full, handing unlimited repairs to whoever needed them most. concede is now capped at dealt minus healed, and Refactor requires that much to exist: the cost is progress, which is finite.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: 'This costs something' is not the same as 'this is bounded'. A cost only limits an action if the currency can run out and the thing being protected depends on that currency. I had the right instinct -- price it -- and picked a currency with no floor, in a system where the resource that matters is a different one. Worth asking of any cost: what happens when the player has spent all of it? If the answer is 'nothing changes', it was never a cost.

decisions.decision: Refactor is priced in damage already dealt, not in boss health
decisions.rationale: M56. HP cannot end a fight and is unspendable past full, so it is not a bound. Progress is finite, and pricing in it makes the player who has achieved nothing exactly the one who cannot buy immunity.

decisions.decision: The mutators live on Fight; the prices live on the abilities
alternatives: Let abilities manipulate Fight's private fields directly
decisions.rationale: The arithmetic that must stay consistent stays with the state it constrains, and every mutator clamps to what the fight can afford.

decisions.decision: use reports the price actually paid
decisions.rationale: Every mutator clamps, so the two can differ. An ability announcing a cost the fight could not meet would be lying on the screen.

decisions.decision: Steady Hand needs two repairs before it may be used
decisions.rationale: Spending your last repair to make a repair you can no longer afford free is a trap rather than a choice.

decisions.decision: Overclock empties the pool rather than reducing it
decisions.rationale: A version that kept one is a free bonus. Emptying it makes the ability a decision about whether the fight is already over.

decisions.decision: --ability follows --fix's precedent for scripting an interactive choice
alternatives: An interactive menu in the repair pane
decisions.rationale: A menu is W11's territory once there is an earned loadout to choose from, and building one now would invent W11's gate early.

friction.description: Wiring the abilities into the live fight and then finding the path unreachable from a test. _spend_ability fires when the pool empties and a repair mechanism is available, and the mechanism needs a real terminal on both streams -- so a piped fight ends for lack of a repair pane rather than for lack of repairs, and the ability correctly never gets a turn. Same gap Q85 already names rather than a new one, and the placement is right for real play, so the function is driven directly instead.

handoff.state: T4 W1-W10 LANDED. Only W11 remains. Abilities act on a fight's resources at a stated cost, and a full loadout still loses -- checked by removing a cost and watching seven tests fail. Exit criteria 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 verified; 3 verified for the two simulated players who can fail (Q89). 1312 tests green unpinned, 1288 pinned, verify clean on 54 reference runs.
handoff.next_action: T4 W11, earning and equipping: which abilities a class unlocks and at what mastery. The trajectory calls it 'the only place the two layers are allowed to meet, and they meet as a gate, never as an average', which is the whole design constraint -- a class may decide which ability, mastery may decide whether, and nothing may combine them into a number. Criterion 8 is the one at risk and it is currently verified.
